name: Kals am Großglockner
kurzbeschreibung: Key starting point for ascending the Großglockner via the famous Kalser Höhenweg.
beschreibung:
Overview

Kals am Großglockner is situated at an elevation of 1,324 metres in the Kals Valley within the district of Lienz, East Tyrol, majestically cradled at the foot of Mount Großglockner (3,798 m)—Austria's highest mountain. Covering an expansive territory of roughly 180 square kilometres in the core zone of the Hohe Tauern National Park, the municipality is home to approximately 1,110 residents distributed across traditional hamlets including Ködnitz, Großdorf, and Lesach. Celebrated worldwide as the historic cradle of Eastern Alpine mountaineering, Kals serves as the prime launching pad for ascents of the Großglockner via the classic south route and the legendary Stüdlgrat ridge. Encircled by the glaciated peaks of the Glockner and Schober ranges, Kals seamlessly harmonises pristine high-alpine wilderness, living mountain heritage, and refined eco-friendly tourism.

History

The name Kals originates from the Slavic root kal, denoting marshy or alluvial ground along the riverbed. The community was first documented in 1197 as an established parish under the Prince-Archbishops of Salzburg. Kals carved its name into mountaineering lore on July 28, 1800, when local carpenters Martin and Sepp Klotz stood among the team achieving the historic first ascent of Mount Großglockner. In 1869, Prague merchant and mountaineering visionary Johann Stüdl founded the first mountain guide association of the Eastern Alps in Kals, funding the construction of the famed Stüdlhütte at 2,801 metres. The Parish Church of St. Rupert in Ködnitz was consecrated in 1516, featuring a Gothic fortified bell tower and neoclassical extensions from 1818. The Glocknerhaus Museum hosts the celebrated exhibition "Under the Spell of the Großglockner," detailing two centuries of alpine conquests.

Getting There

Kals am Großglockner benefits from good road and public transit links. Motorists approaching from the north (Salzburg, Germany) take the scenic Felbertauern highway B108 past Mittersill and Matrei in Osttirol to Huben in the Isel Valley, where the L26 Kals provincial road climbs 14 kilometres into the valley. Arriving from the south (Carinthia, Italy), follow the B108 northward from Lienz to Huben and turn onto the L26. Rail passengers arrive at Lienz railway station along the Drau Valley Railway. Outside the station, regular VVT regional bus route 952 operates direct daily services into Kals, stopping in Ködnitz, Großdorf, and Taurer.

Tips

A journey up the toll-operated Kalser Glocknerstraße road to the Lucknerhaus alpine lodge at 1,920 metres is essential, offering staggering vistas of the Großglockner's southern precipices and serving as the trailhead for ascents to the Stüdlhütte and Adlersruhe refuge. In winter, the Großglockner Resort Kals-Matrei forms East Tyrol's largest ski area, boasting 44 kilometres of slopes and the chic Adler Lounge perched at 2,421 metres. In summer, hike through the rugged Daberklamm gorge into the Dorfertal valley toward the emerald-green Dorfersee alpine lake, or tackle multi-day treks along the Kalser High Trail.
